**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.project_role_capabilities`

**One row is** What one project role may do — one row per (project_role, capability). The project layer of the four-layer resolver, shaped exactly like `role_capabilities` so all four layers read the same way.

Seeded by WP 2.2 with the split that gives `analyst` its meaning: an analyst may edit tier-4 decisions (`data_edit_policies`) and may NOT edit the tier-2 measured inputs those decisions are judged against (`data_edit_inputs`). Before the split one `data_editing` flag governed both, so the role could not exist.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — **1 with no predicate** |

Read is open to everyone (`USING (true)`): it is a static policy table with no per-tenant content, and every client needs it to render what a role can do. As with the other capability tables there is no write policy, so writes are service-role only.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 1 policy here grants access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `project_role_capabilities: read all` — `SELECT`
>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

**Substitutions** — every point where a value you did not supply can stand in
for one you did.

| When | The value used | Shown as | Visible where |
|---|---|---|---|
| no row exists for this (project_role, capability) | the org layer's answer, then the role layer's, then false | `default` | capabilities_for_user returns the resolved boolean; the layer that decided it is not currently reported |

> WHICH LAYER DECIDED IS NOT RETURNED, and that is a §5 T1 gap worth naming: a user told "you cannot export" cannot learn whether that came from their role, their org, their project role or an explicit user deny. The resolver has the information and discards it. WP 2.4 renders governance and is the place to fix it.
